subject: CAIQ: config-drift attestation timeline & evidence routing
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@olivehealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: security@olivehealth.com
Date: 2028-09-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: CAIQ follow-up — control evidence for configuration drift

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we finish filling out the CAIQ, a couple of our control owners flagged the configuration-drift / immutable-infrastructure controls (CCM: INF-3, CM-4 equivalent) and asked for two concrete pieces of evidence:

- a short-run sample showing a drift detection alert (timestamped) and the remediation/rollback activity;
- the owner attestation timeline for the past 90 days that shows who is responsible for config management and when attestations were recorded.

Can you point us to where we keep the sample artifacts (we prefer a small archive we can download) and provide an owner attestation cadence (or a simple CSV export) so we can attach it to the CAIQ answers? Also: are there any known caveats for ephemeral k8s clusters (we run a short-lived batch cluster model)?

If easiest, we can hop on a 30-min call next week with our control owner + auditor (Jamie from CloudAudit). Proposed times: Tue 9/12 10–11am PT or Wed 9/13 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Patel
Security Manager, OliveHealth
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@olivehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-11T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up — control evidence for configuration drift

Samira —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can provide both items and a concise explanation for ephemeral clusters. I've attached an annotated CAIQ crosswalk and a small evidence sample to this thread to kickoff. High-level plan:

1) Evidence archive: provides a drift alert (controller reconciler diff + alerting event) and the rollback entry from our infra-ops runbook. See attachment: caiq-annotated-crosswalk-OLIVE-v1.xlsx (tab: INF-3).

2) Owner attestations: we keep attestations in an internal attestations table and can export a CSV of the last 90 days for your reviewers. We'll surface a simple owners.csv and a brief narrative explaining the attestation process.

3) Ephemeral clusters: for short-lived k8s clusters we snapshot reconcilers and use our controller ID + cluster-id binding to map alerts back to the owning service. The sample archive includes a sample reconciler diff and cluster metadata that demonstrates traceability. The key caveat is retention window — by default metrics/logs are retained 30 days; we can pull a longer retention export if you need 90+ days.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will upload the Terraform state snapshot and SIEM query results to the Drive folder and send a one‑page attestation CSV by EOD 9/12.
- Kimberly (copied) will coordinate with your auditor to set the 30-minute walkthrough if the proposed times work.

If that plan sounds OK, I’ll proceed.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Evidence upload: Terraform state + SIEM exports (CAIQ INF-3)

Samira / Jamie —

Uploading the evidence bundle we discussed. Contents are in the Drive folder linked below and attached here as small stubs for your convenience. Attachments include: terraform-state-snapshot-20280910.json and siem-query-results-20280909.csv. The crosswalk (caiq-annotated-crosswalk-OLIVE-v1.xlsx) maps each CAIQ question to the artifact name and the internal owner.

Notes and clarifications (technical):
- The drift alert in the sample is a controller reconciliation diff that produced alert id ALRT-20280909-77; that alert triggered an automated rollback via our reconciliation controller. The reconciler diff and the rollback job log are inside config-drift-sample-20280910.tar.gz (path: /alerts/ALRT-20280909-77/*).
- Terraform snapshot is a read-only export of the state for the affected resource group and includes instance metadata with cluster-id tags. We strip any user PII before export.
- SIEM query is a saved lookup (query id: siem-q-2028-09-09) for alert correlations — the CSV is a redacted sample showing event timestamps and correlation keys.

Where we put things: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aZq-example-evidence-folder (readers: samira.patel@olivehealth.com, jamie@cloudaudit.com).

HubSpot reference: OLIVE-2237 (useful for your procurement/audit tracker).

If you or Jamie need any further breakdown (e.g., JSON diffs per reconciler) we can produce a short tailored export. Happy to discuss on the 9/12 walkthrough at 10:30am PT.
